items.title: Name company behind Puchong slaughterhouse raid, says Radzi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A member of parliament has called on the authorities to disclose the name of the company behind a slaughterhouse raided for breaching halal certification rules. Putrajaya MP Datuk Dr Mohd Radzi Jidin also called for the investigation into the company to be expedited. "I am still waiting for the authorities to reveal the name of the company that runs the chicken processing facility raided in Puchong," he said in a Facebook post.

items.title: Melaka polls: All 28 candidate nomination centres close at 10am
items.summary: MELAKA: The nomination process for the Melaka election has been completed after all 28 nomination centres across the state closed at 10am. The one-hour process for submitting nomination papers began at 9am, before the returning officers announced its closure at their respective centres. Checks at several nomination centres since early this morning found supporters accompanying their respective party candidates in an orderly manner.

items.title: Flavio Bolsonaro says he left Brazil because he is the victim of 'persecution'
items.summary: BRASILIA: Former conservative presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro said on Friday that he fled Brazil for the United States because he was a victim of "persecution" in his country. Bolsonaro, who lost Sunday's election runoff to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, secretly left Brazil on Tuesday and arrived in Florida aboard a private jet on Wednesday after travelling through Argentina and Ecuador. he said of his father.

items.title: Man suffers broken leg in suspected hit-and-run over loan dispute in Johor
items.summary: Iskandar Puteri district police chief Assistant Commissioner Radin Ramlan Radin Taha said police received a report on the incident, which occurred in front of a supermarket, at 6.38pm. Following the incident, police arrested three people, comprising a man and two women aged between 34 and 53. Radin Ramlan said police also seized a Proton Saga and were tracking down several others believed to be involved in the incident.

items.title: Melaka polls: Tok Mat accompanies BN's Lendu candidate to nomination centre
items.summary: MELAKA: Barisan Nasional candidate for the Lendu seat Datuk Abdul Hakim Abdul Wahid arrived at the nomination centre for the Melaka election at 9.14am. Abdul Hakim, who is also political secretary to Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, arrived at the Alor Gajah Youth Complex wearing a blue Baju Melayu and accompanied by BN deputy chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan. Meanwhile, Bersatu candidate Nazri Ramli arrived earlier, about 8.50am, wearing a red Baju Melayu and accompanied by the party's co-founder Datuk Seri Mohd Redzuan Md Yusof.

items.title: Loan dispute turns violent in Skudai: Man’s leg broken after being rammed by car, three held
items.summary: Iskandar Puteri district police chief Assistant Commissioner Radin Ramlan Radin Taha said police received a report on the incident at 6.38pm yesterday, Sinar Harian reported. “In the incident, a 35-year-old local man suffered a broken right leg following an incident involving a car driven by one of the individuals involved. Radin Ramlan said police detained three locals, a man and two women aged between 34 and 53, to assist in investigations.

items.title: Melaka polls: Sanusi turns up to back Pas candidate in Paya Rumput
items.summary: MELAKA: Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor turned up at Hang Jebat Stadium today to accompany Pas candidate for the Paya Rumput seat Rafie Ahmad. Sanusi, who is also PN election director, was seen alongside Rafie as Perikatan Nasional stepped up its campaign efforts in the constituency. The agreement was signed by Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki and PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan, who is also Pas secretary-general, with BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi witnessing the ceremony.

items.title: Melaka polls: 'Uncle Wong', 'Dak Nor' show up for BN's Duyong candidate's nomination
items.summary: MELAKA: A lively atmosphere greeted incumbent Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem as he arrived at about 8.35am today at the Duyong state constituency nomination centre for the 16th Melaka state election. UMNO secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki was also present at the nomination centre to accompany Mohd Noor Helmy. In the 15th Melaka state election, Mohd Noor Helmy scored an upset victory over then-incumbent Damian Yeo Shen Li, winning by a slim majority of 200 votes.

items.title: Hadi's presence boosts PN candidate's morale in Bukit Katil
items.summary: MELAKA: Perikatan Nasional candidate Muhammad Ridzuan Mohd Sarif received a morale boost from the presence of Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang during his first appearance as a candidate. Ridzuan, a Pas Hang Tuah Jaya division committee member, was accompanied by several coalition leaders, including PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan and Parti Pejuang Tanah Air (Pejuang) president Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir. Also present were MP Datuk Seri Dr Shahidan Kassim and Alor Setar MP Afnan Hamimi Taib Azamudden.

items.title: Melaka polls: Four parties bring colourful atmosphere to Klebang nomination centre
items.summary: MELAKA: Supporters of four political parties turned up in large numbers at the Klebang Japerun Complex here today, creating a colourful atmosphere ahead of nomination for the Klebang seat. Supporters of Pakatan Harapan, Barisan Nasional, Bersatu and Bersama began gathering as early as 7.30am, waving party flags and banners while wearing their respective party colours. Several party leaders were also present to accompany their candidates, including MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong and Bersama co-founder Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli.

items.title: Daylight robbery at a Damansara Damai jeweller, RM300,000 gone
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — A man armed with a sharp weapon robbed a jewellery shop in Damansara Damai, Petaling Jaya, yesterday afternoon, resulting in losses estimated at RM300,000. Petaling Jaya district police chief ACP Shamsudin Mamat said police were alerted to the robbery at 1.19 pm. Shamsudin urged anyone with information about the incident to contact the nearest police station or the Petaling Jaya District Police Headquarters operations room at 03-7966 2222 to assist in investigations.

items.title: Supporters out by 7am as Melaka candidates file their papers
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 31 — All 28 nomination centres for the 16th Melaka State Election opened simultaneously at 9 am today. The Election Commission (EC) has set November 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, with early voting scheduled for November 10. For the latest updates on the 16th Melaka State Election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/.

items.title: Macron to visit Malaysia on Nov 16–17 as ties with France deepen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — French President Emmanuel Macron is expected to visit Malaysia on November 16–17, said Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin. He said the relationship between Malaysia and France has reached another level following Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s visit to France last year, noting that Anwar has established a very good relationship with Macron. “Datuk Seri Anwar visited France last year and subsequently invited President Macron to visit Malaysia.

items.title: Melaka polls: Azman first to arrive at Paya Rumput nomination centre
items.summary: MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan candidate for the Paya Rumput seat Datuk Azman Abidin was the first to arrive at the nomination centre today, reaching Hang Jebat Stadium about 8.40am. Azman, who is the political secretary to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, arrived ahead of the nomination process for the Paya Rumput seat in the 16th Melaka election. More than 200 PH supporters turned up for Azman as early as 7.30am The supporters were accompanied by PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, who was present at Hang Jebat Stadium here, to lend his support to Azman as the coalition stepped up its campaign efforts in the constituency.

items.title: Islamic affairs minister backs making intoxicated drivers pay victims’ families, cites ‘diya’ study can be guide
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — A study on ‘Diat’ or compensation published by the Federal Territory Mufti’s Office can serve as a reference in detailing compensation payments to victims or next of kin involved in accidents caused by drivers under the influence of alcohol or drugs. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the research could provide guidance for proposed amendments to the Road Transport Act 1987 (Act 333) to mandate that drivers under the influence of alcohol or drugs who cause accidents pay compensation to victims or their heirs. He said his department fully supports the government’s efforts to amend the act, as announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim during the tabling of Budget 2027 on October 9.

items.title: Damansara Damai jewellery shop loses RM300,000 in robbery
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A man armed with a sharp weapon robbed a jewellery shop in Damansara Damai, Petaling Jaya, yesterday afternoon, resulting in losses estimated at RM300,000. Petaling Jaya police chief assistant commissioner Shamsudin Mamat said police were alerted to the robbery at 1.19pm. Those with information can contact the nearest police station or the Petaling Jaya district police headquarters at 03-7966 2222.

items.title: Melaka polls: Sea of blue and red supporters gather at Tanjung Bidara
items.summary: MELAKA: A sea of supporters dressed in blue and red gathered at Dewan Datuk KPT (B) Haji Ab Karim, Japerun Tanjung Bidara, here this morning as Barisan Nasional and Pakatan Harapan candidates arrived for nomination for the Tanjung Bidara seat. BN supporters, dressed in blue, began gathering as early as 7am before marching about 100 metres while waving party flags and chanting "blue wave" slogans as they accompanied caretaker Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh to the nomination centre. Ab Rauf, who is also state BN chairman, arrived at 8.58am accompanied by BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.

items.title: Melaka polls: Party cheers, chants mark nomination day in Machap Jaya
items.summary: echoed around the Japerun Machap Jaya Complex as Pakatan Harapan (PH) supporters accompanied the coalition's candidate, Datuk Ginie Lim Siew Lin, to the nomination centre for the 16th Melaka state election. Also accompanying the PH candidate were PH secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, PKR vice-president Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, PKR Wanita chief Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek and PKR International Bureau director Dr Maszlee Malik. Machap Jaya Prasanth!"

items.title: IGP says ex-border control chief Shuhaily’s PDRM comeback hinges on AGC advice and royal consent
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — The new assignment of Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain in the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) will only be determined after obtaining the consent of His Majesty, Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia to allow his tenure as Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) director-general to be ended prematurely. Inspector-General of Police (IGP) Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said Mohd Shuhaily’s appointment to the post had previously received the consent of His Majesty, as he is a police cadre officer. Commenting further on the duties and follow-up action involving Mohd Shuhaily after his return to PDRM, Mohd Khalid said no decision had been made so far.

items.title: Selangor’s Bersatu deal: Just a few ‘sensitive details’ left, says state Pakatan chief
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 31 — A decision regarding the Confidence and Supply Agreement (CSA) between the Selangor State Government and Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) is expected to be announced in the near future once all negotiation details are finalised. Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said that negotiations with Bersatu are ongoing and a foundational understanding has been reached, though several sensitive matters still need to be refined. He noted that the cooperation established at the Federal level has facilitated efforts to implement a similar approach in Selangor to ensure state administrative stability.

items.title: A different kind of buzz at Bukit Katil nomination centre
items.summary: MELAKA: A nomination centre is usually abuzz with political supporters rallying behind their candidates, but the scene at Dewan Tun Ali in Bukit Katil today offered a different spectacle, with a children's football match and preparations for a wedding reception adding to the activity. While candidates and supporters gathered for the nomination process for the 16th Melaka state election, children were busy chasing the ball on the football field, while a marquee was being set up nearby for a wedding reception. Meanwhile, preparations for the wedding reception continued with a large tent set up near the nomination centre, adding to the unusual scene on nomination day.

items.title: Police liaising with Pakistani authorities over 130 Malaysians detained in scam raid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bukit Aman is liaising with Pakistani authorities through the Foreign Ministry to obtain further details about a raid on a suspected cyber scam centre in Rawalpindi, Pakistan. "We still need assistance from the Pakistani authorities to obtain all the relevant details," he said after attending an appreciation dinner organised by the Malaysian Ex-Police Association last night. On the identities of those detained, he said police had yet to receive a complete list from Pakistani authorities.

items.title: BN, PH leaders rally behind candidates in Ayer Molek
items.summary: MELAKA: Two leaders from parties in the unity government arrived at the Ayer Molek Japerun Complex here to accompany and show their support for their respective candidates contesting the Ayer Molek seat on nomination day today. Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, who is also Investment, Trade and Industry Minister, arrived about 8.30am to accompany Barisan Nasional candidate Datuk Mohd Ridhwan Mohd Ali. [[nid:1567418]] The Ayer Molek seat is expected to see a straight fight between Ridhwan and Hakimin.

items.title: Police probe hacking of Kluang council LED screens after obscene content displayed
items.summary: KLUANG, Oct 31 — Eight LED display screens belonging to the Kluang Municipal Council (MPK) around the town are believed to have been hacked to show obscene content on Thursday, according to Berita Harian . Kluang district police chief Assistant Commissioner Bahrin Mohd Noh said police received a report on the incident from a 42-year-old local man yesterday. He said initial investigations found the complainant had been alerted by his staff before receiving several WhatsApp messages containing screenshots and video recordings of the obscene content on the screens.

items.title: Seven candidates, seven seats: DAP’s Melaka game plan
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 31 — DAP aims to defend the four seats it currently holds in the 16th Melaka State Election, namely Kesidang, Kota Laksamana, Bandar Hilir and Ayer Keroh. DAP National Election Director Wong Kah Woh said the party was also eyeing three additional seats allocated to it by Pakatan Harapan (PH), namely Gadek, Duyong and Pengkalan Batu. The Deputy Education Minister said DAP’s nationwide election machinery would be deployed in phases to assist the party’s seven candidates, with the campaign coordinated by Melaka DAP chairman Khoo Poay Tiong.

items.title: Aini Ideris, UPM’s first woman vice-chancellor, crowned National Academic Figure
items.summary: KLANG, Oct 31 — Former Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) vice-chancellor Prof Emeritus Datuk Dr Aini Ideris was named National Academic Figure at the 17th National Academic Awards (AAN) ceremony here yesterday. The award was presented by Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir at a hotel here, with Dr Aini also receiving a trophy, certificate and RM200,000 in prize money. The Promising Academic Award went to Prof Dr Ong Wee Jun of Xiamen University Malaysia (XMUM) and Associate Prof Dr Serene Lock Sow Mun of Universiti Teknologi Petronas (UTP).

items.title: Melaka polls: Amirudin joins over 200 PH supporters to support Azman
items.summary: MELAKA: More than 200 Pakatan Harapan (PH) supporters gathered in Paya Rumput today to back the coalition's candidate, Datuk Azman Abidin, in the 16th Melaka state election. Jun Lye Chye Yoon, 51, who has lived in Paya Rumput for 18 years, said she trusted Azman because of his close working relationship with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. In the 2021 state election, BN's Datuk Rais Yasin retained Paya Rumput with a majority of 629 votes after securing 6,830 votes.

items.title: AirBorneo launches direct Kuching-Jakarta route from Nov 13, three flights weekly
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 31 — AirBorneo today opened ticket sales for its new direct service between Kuching and Jakarta, with all-in one-way fares starting from RM399 in Economy Class and RM888 in Business Class. Flight MY 396 departs Kuching at 3.10pm, while the return flight, MY 397, leaves Jakarta at 4.55pm local time. “Our direct Kuching to Jakarta service marks an important milestone as we grow AirBorneo’s regional network across key Asean gateways,” AirBorneo chief executive officer Megat Ardian Aminuddin said in a statement.

items.title: Nomination day is here: Melaka’s 14-day campaign starts today
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 31 — The 16th Melaka State Election officially begins today, with the nomination process taking place simultaneously at 28 nomination centres across the state from 9 am. Prospective candidates have until 10 am to submit their nomination papers to the Election Returning Officers before the list of eligible candidates is officially announced. The EC has set November 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, with early voting scheduled for November 10.

items.title: Teen, 14, arrested for throwing stone that shattered KTMB train window in Arau
items.summary: The suspect, a local secondary school student, was detained today under Op Cantas by the Arau district Criminal Investigation Division together with the Arau police station task force. Arau district police chief Superintendent Ahmad Mohsin Md Rodi said initial investigations found the suspect had admitted to deliberately throwing a stone at the train while at the Kampung Jelempok motorcycle overpass. The report was lodged at the Arau police station at 12.30pm yesterday.

items.title: Pakatan wants 18 seats in Melaka, and to keep the five it already has
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 31 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is targeting victory in 18 of the 24 seats it will contest in the Melaka state election, including retaining the five seats it previously won. Melaka PKR acting chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim was also present. For the latest news on the 16th Melaka State Election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/.

items.title: Melaka polls: Bersama's Aliza arrives first as Adly Zahari set to defend Bukit Katil
items.summary: BUKIT KATIL: Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) candidate for the N17 Bukit Katil seat, Dr Aliza Che Amran, arrived at the nomination centre at Dewan Tun Ali. The other candidates are incumbent and Melaka Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Adly Zahari and Perikatan Nasional (PN) candidate Muhammad Ridzuan Mohd Sarif. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Sabah public bus ridership jumps 208pct in two months
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Ridership on Kota Kinabalu's public bus service has surged by 208 per cent in two months, said Sabah Commercial Vehicle Licensing Board (CVLB) chairman Datuk Phoong Jin Zhe. "These figures are very encouraging and prove that the people of Sabah genuinely need a better public transport system. The BAS.MY service, also known as the "Pink Bus", was officially launched a few months ago and covers stops at Queen Elizabeth Hospital I and II, as well as Kota Kinabalu International Airport.

items.title: Melaka polls: Different party colours, one breakfast table
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: Supporters of Barisan Nasional (BN), Pakatan Harapan (PH), Perikatan Nasional (PN) and Bersama put their political differences aside to share a breakfast stall today. They gathered ahead of the nomination process for the Machap Jaya state seat at Kompleks Japerun Machap Jaya. PH supporters in red, BN supporters in blue and Bersama supporters in yellow were seen at the stall, alongside PN supporters who also took the opportunity to have breakfast before the nomination process began.

items.title: Start small and save early with PTPTN
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Parents should start saving for their children's education early, even if they can only afford small amounts, to prepare for future higher education costs. As the world marks World Savings Day today, the National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) is encouraging families to make saving a regular habit and plan ahead for their children's education. She said parents should not wait until their children were approaching university age before setting aside money for higher education.

items.title: Malaysia may hit four-year growth high as HSBC lifts 2026 forecast [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's economy could post its strongest annual growth in four years after HSBC raised its 2026 gross domestic product (GDP) forecast to 5.5 per cent from 5.2 per cent, a revision that economists say is plausible. HSBC said the upgrade followed Malaysia's better-than-expected advance GDP growth estimate of 5.3 per cent for the third quarter (Q3). The bank also raised its Q4 growth forecast to 5.3 per cent from 4.7 per cent, suggesting that economic momentum would continue through the end of the year.

items.title: PH-Bersatu clashes in Melaka could benefit BN, PN – Analysts
items.summary: Universiti Utara Malaysia political analyst Prof Dr Azizuddin Mohd Sani said the absence of a formal electoral pact between PH and Bersatu meant multi-cornered contests were to be expected. He said the outcome would inevitably lead to vote-splitting, potentially benefiting BN and PN. Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) political analyst Prof Dr Mujibu Abd Muis said the overlapping contests demonstrated that parties could function as parliamentary partners while remaining direct electoral rivals.

items.title: Top EU diplomat says Lavrov presented 'lies' at G20 talks
items.summary: ATLANTA: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov presented "lies" during G20 talks on the Ukraine conflict, the EU's foreign policy chief told AFP on Friday, accusing Moscow of being unprepared for peace negotiations. "We were talking about the big geopolitical crises, including Ukraine, and we were able to address Sergei Lavrov head-on with this," Kaja Kallas said on the sidelines of a G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, Georgia. But Russia does not appear ready to move ahead with peace talks, Kallas said.

items.title: 16th Melaka election kicks off with nomination process today [WATCH]
items.summary: MELAKA: The 16th Melaka election officially begins today, with the nomination process taking place simultaneously at 28 nomination centres across the state from 9am. Prospective candidates have until 10am to submit their nomination papers to the election returning officers, before the list of eligible candidates is officially announced. The EC has set Nov 14 as polling day for the Melaka election, with early voting scheduled for Nov 10.

items.title: E-waste trade driven by value of precious metals in discarded devices
items.summary: PORT KLANG: A discarded computer or electronic device may have reached the end of its useful life, but the materials inside it can still command a price. Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) Port Klang commander Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal said printed circuit boards (PCBs) could contain precious metals, including gold, silver and palladium. Lead is also among the materials identified.

items.title: Following the money trail behind Malaysia's e-waste trade
items.summary: PORT KLANG: Authorities are tracing the financial and physical networks behind Malaysia's e-waste trade, with hundreds of abandoned containers linked to anti-money laundering investigations and enforcement teams targeting suspected illegal storage facilities inland. Of the 1,257 containers abandoned at Port Klang in 2024 and 2025, 772 were linked to police investigations, 375 were handled by the Customs Department and 112 by the Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA). MCBA Port Klang commander Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal said police were investigating 772 containers under the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001.

items.title: Russia uncompromising as Rubio hosts G20 talks in shadow of conflicts
items.summary: ATLANTA: Russia showed no sign on Friday of softening its stance on Kyiv as G20 foreign ministers opened talks in the United States, with the wars in Ukraine and Iran deepening rifts between members of the sprawling forum. Sharp disagreements emerged around the table, with EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas accusing Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov of presenting "lies" on issues such as the conflict in Ukraine. Lavrov, in turn, was "quite provocative" in his remarks, a European diplomatic source said.

items.title: Malaysia widens e-waste crackdown beyond Port Klang [WATCH]
items.summary: PORT KLANG: More than 31,000 tonnes of electronic waste packed into 1,257 containers were abandoned at Port Klang, prompting a multi-agency crackdown that has expanded beyond the port to suspected illegal storage and processing facilities inland. Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) Port Klang joint task force records show that the 1,257 containers were abandoned in 2024 and 2025, with their contents estimated to weigh 31,475 tonnes. MCBA Port Klang commander Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal said the operation involved close cooperation between enforcement agencies to clear the backlog and take action against those responsible.

items.title: NST CRIME WATCH: Dead baby in bin, another abandoned; murder probe and custody death draw scrutiny [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: One baby was found dead in a rubbish bin while another was found abandoned beneath a staircase. In Kota Tinggi, Johor, a 68-year-old Felda settler was found axed to death. A death in custody at the Cheras district police headquarters also drew the attention of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

items.title: Friends, foes and four awkward clashes: Who’s teaming up with whom in the Melaka polls?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Former rivals Umno and PAS are joining forces to contest the Melaka state election, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) and Bersatu are exploring an electoral understanding — despite preparing to fight each other in four constituencies. PH, meanwhile, is seeking common ground with Bersatu even as the latter’s relationship with its PN partners, particularly PAS, continues to deteriorate. BN-PN: United for Melaka The clearest electoral arrangement in Melaka is between BN, led by Umno, and PN, with PAS playing a central role in the cooperation.

items.title: Malaysian doctor Mary Suma Cardosa makes history as first Asian to lead global pain research body
items.summary: In a statement issued by IASP, she said her presidency would focus on advancing pain science, strengthening healthcare education and improving access to effective pain management worldwide. “Pain affects people in every country, but access to effective pain care remains profoundly unequal,” she said, highlighting the importance of education, stronger clinical services and multidisciplinary cooperation. An anaesthesiologist with more than three decades of experience in pain medicine, Cardosa has played a pivotal role in developing Malaysia’s pain management services and strengthening pain education in the country and across Southeast Asia.

items.title: Paws off! Shah Alam High Court rules condo management cannot impose blanket pet bans
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 30 — The High Court here today ruled that a joint management body (JMB) cannot impose a blanket ban on keeping pets in private residential units through its house rules. They said the court ruled that the mere presence of pets in a residential unit did not constitute a breach of house rules and that any enforcement action must be based on By-law 14 of the Strata Management (Maintenance and Management) Regulations 2015 and supported by evidence. House Rule 9.0 cannot be used to prohibit or penalise Ms Noraseela merely for keeping her three cats; Enforcement must be evidence-based.

items.title: RM3 for extra soup? Labuan eatery compounded for failing to display charge on menu
items.summary: LABUAN, Oct 30 — An eatery operator here was compounded after charging an additional RM3 for a serving of soup that was not listed on the restaurant’s displayed price menu. KPDN Labuan director Junaidah Arbain said the action followed a consumer complaint lodged through the ministry’s e-Aduan portal, with an inspection at about 10am finding that the displayed price list included additional charges for rice and noodles but did not specify the price of extra soup. “Following the non-compliance detected, we issued a compound to the operator under the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering (Price Marking for Goods and Charges for Services) Order 2020, under the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering Act 2011,” she told Bernama today.

items.title: Foreign investments should deliver more opportunities for Malaysian SMEs, says Steven Sim
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 30 — The government wants local content to be given greater consideration in government, government-linked company (GLC) and multinational corporation (MNC) procurements to create more opportunities for local micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). “We also want government procurements, GLC procurements and, of course, MNC procurements to have a perspective for local content. So, there must be a requirement for local contents,” he said.

items.title: Eleventh-hour boost for MCA: Perikatan returns Kota Laksamana, bringing Melaka seat tally to four
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 30 — MCA has announced that it will contest one more state seat in the 16th Melaka state election, after Kota Laksamana was returned to Barisan Nasional (BN) by Perikatan Nasional (PN). MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong said Melvin Chua will be fielded as the candidate, following discussions between BN and PN after the latter indicated that MCA is better suited to contest the seat. The addition of Kota Laksamana means MCA will contest four seats, including Machap Jaya, Kelebang and Bandar Hilir.

items.title: Sabah defence upgrades not a response to Philippine military build-up, says Khaled
items.summary: LABUAN, Oct 30 — Malaysia will continue strengthening its military capabilities in Sabah to safeguard national security amid regional geopolitical developments, but the move is not a direct response to the Philippines’ military build-up on Balabac Island, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said. “Every country has the right to strengthen its military capabilities, and Malaysia will do the same. Khaled said strengthening Malaysia’s defence capabilities, particularly in Sabah, remained a key priority of the Defence Ministry.

items.title: The more, the merrier? State Pakatan chairman says crowded Melaka races could work in coalition’s favour
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 30 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) does not regard multi-cornered contests in the Melaka state election as a disadvantage, saying a crowded field could instead create more opportunities for the coalition to secure victories. Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said a straight fight did not necessarily give a party an advantage, as three- or four-cornered contests could, in certain circumstances, offer better prospects from a strategic standpoint. Also present was Melaka PKR chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim.

items.title: MOF never ordered rural road projects cancelled, only deferred new contracts, says Tengku Zafrul
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — The Finance Ministry (MOF) has never issued any directive to cancel rural road projects, but has only deferred new contracts to prevent outstanding payments to contractors from continuing to accumulate, according to the prime minister’s senior political adviser, Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Tengku Abdul Aziz. He said the deferment was necessary following rural road development expenditure exceeding the original allocations approved by Parliament annually since 2022, resulting in increased contractual commitments and outstanding payments to contractors. “In Sabah and Sarawak alone, actual rural road expenditure this year reached RM1.41 billion, the highest in the past 10 years.

items.title: Saris, sweets and shopping sprees: Deepavali buzz builds across Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — The festive atmosphere ahead of Deepavali on November 8 is becoming more vibrant as the Indian community nationwide begins making preparations for the Festival of Lights, including purchasing traditional attire, preparing special delicacies and decorating their homes to celebrate the occasion with family and relatives. Another visitor, N. Rama Rao, 38, said Little India remains his family’s preferred shopping destination as it offers a wide selection of traditional attire at reasonable prices. Shoppers browse traditional attire, accessories and festive decorations ahead of Deepavali in Johor Bahru October 30, 2026.

items.title: Rubbish raid! Thirteen-foot crocodile caught after rummaging through trash for food in Sarawak village
items.summary: KOTA SAMARAHAN, Oct 30 — A crocodile measuring over 13 feet (about 3.96m) was captured this morning following reports of the reptile roaming in the area and posing a potential safety concern for nearby villagers. Licensed crocodile capture team Sarawak Crocter said in a Facebook post that the operation was carried out in collaboration with the Sarawak Forestry Corporation (SFC). — The Borneo Post

items.title: Bought one thing, got another? Anwar orders crackdown on online shopping scams, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 30 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) and the Communications Ministry, through the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), to take immediate action against fraud and scams on e-commerce platforms. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the directive followed Anwar’s concerns over problems faced by online shoppers and sellers, including high commission fees imposed on merchants and customers receiving products that did not match their orders. “The prime minister raised concerns about the problems faced by e-commerce users, particularly high fees and commissions charged to sellers, as well as customers receiving products that differ from what they ordered.

items.title: Repairs on Kuching’s Jalan Lapangan Terbang water main completed, supply restoration in stages, says Sarawak Water
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 30 — Emergency repair works on a critical 750mm mild steel cement-lined (MSCL) water main on Jalan Lapangan Terbang were completed at 2am today, said Sarawak Water Sdn Bhd. The utility provider said water supply restoration is now underway in stages. Following completion of the repair works at 2am, Sarawak Water said valve reopening and network pressurisation had commenced, with water supply expected to be restored gradually.

items.title: Sale of first industrial plots on Silicon Island to start in Q1 2027, says Penang CM
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 30 — The Penang government hopes to sell the first industrial plots on Silicon Island as early as the first quarter of 2027, said Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow. He said the development on Silicon Island will focus on the 700-acre Green Tech Park which is planned as a green, smart and sustainable high-tech industrial hub in line with environmental, social and governance (ESG) principles. He said the first factory in the Green Tech Park is expected to begin operations by 2028 while creating high-skilled employment opportunities for Penangites.

items.title: Indonesian woman fined RM4,000 and ordered deported over RM100 sex offer to undercover cop in Kuching
items.summary: Magistrate Nureina Syafika Mohd Najib imposed the sentence against Pita, 37, after she pleaded guilty to a charge under Section 372B of the Penal Code. During the inspection of an unnumbered room, police found Pita with the undercover agent and arrested her for further action. Investigations found that Pita had offered sexual services to the undercover agent for a cash payment of RM100.

items.title: Penang Budget 2027 sets aside RM600 aid for e-hailing drivers, RM500 for newlyweds

He said the state government had disbursed RM57.8 million through the implementation of the first and second phases of the i-Sejahtera programme as at September 30. “As such, in 2027, the Penang State Housing Board (LPNPP) will explore the co-living concept for suitable state government rental housing and People’s Housing Programme units,” he said.
